principles: Original-language source text only; no modern translations.
No cover or illustration assets are imported.
Every selected work must retain an exact provider landing URL, allowlisted TXT source, pinned SHA-256, and prepared chapter count.
Project Gutenberg items must continue to state Public domain in the USA on the exact item landing page.
Gongu items must continue to expose an expired/free-use label and an allowlisted per-item TXT source.
No candidate may be approved or imported merely from this AI-assisted precheck.

us.basis: For pre-1978/restored foreign works, the U.S. Copyright Office states that restored copyright receives the remainder of the term the work would have had, generally 95 years from first publication for pre-1978 published works. The batch requires first publication no later than 1930, so even a restored 1930 work reaches the end of a 95-year term by the end of 2025.

japan.basis: Japan generally uses life plus 70, applies shorter-term reciprocity where the foreign source-country term is shorter, and retains wartime additions for certain Allied works. To avoid relying on a simplistic life+70 calculation, the English cohort is screened to author death year 1944 or earlier; the actual selected cohort currently tops out at 1942.

korea.basis: Korean Copyright Act Article 39 states life plus 70. Article 3(4) provides that a foreign work whose term has expired in its source country does not receive a Korean term. Korean-source candidates are additionally required to be labelled expired/free-use by the Korea Copyright Commission provider.
